item.title: Conformally Calibrated Adaptive Computation in Neural Operators
item.description:
Authors: Abdul Qadir Ibrahim, Martin Burger, Abel Maviano Jonathan

Selecting less computation in a neural operator need not reduce inference time. We study this gap using conformal calibration to choose Fourier modes or channel width per input subject to a fixed error budget. A triangle-inequality envelope bounds all candidates simultaneously; a direct-score rule handles non-monotone candidate errors and, with an input-independent score, calibrates a static baseline under the same marginal guarantee

要点：
- 方法：采用机器学习/深度学习模型。

item.title: From Arraignment to Resolution: Transformer Models of Court Cases
item.description:
Authors: Kory Rosen, Aron Culotta

The criminal legal system is composed of many complex decision points, such as which charges are pursued, how bond is determined, plea deal negotiations, and sentencing. Given the profound impact of such decisions, there is a growing need to increase the transparency within this system. While prior machine learning approaches have focused on modeling single decisions (e.g., recidivism), this paper proposes a transformer-based time series model to forecast the outcome of the next proceeding in a case (e.g., charges accepted, bond set, plea deal made, etc.)

item.title: Entropy-Regularized Integrated Gradients for Stable Feature Attribution
item.description:
Authors: Rukmangadh Sai Myana, Sumit Kumar Jha, Yanzhao Wu

Path-based attribution methods like Integrated Gradients (IG) are widely used to interpret neural networks, yet imperceptible input perturbations can drastically alter their attribution maps while leaving model predictions unchanged. We introduce Entropy-Regularized Integrated Gradients (ERIG), a path-based attribution method that intrinsically attenuates gradient irregularities along the integration path using maximum-entropy softmax weighting with temperature parameter $τ$. item.title: MAIC-2 v2.3: A Fortran program for simulating the surface temperature, atmospheric water transport and surface glaciation of the planet Mars
item.description:
Authors: Ralf Greve, Björn Grieger, Oliver J. Stenzel

The Mars Atmosphere-Ice Coupler MAIC-2 is a computationally efficient, zonally-averaged model designed to simulate Martian surface temperature, atmospheric water transport and surface glaciation over timescales of 10^5 to 10^7 years. While sophisticated General Circulation Models (GCMs) provide high-resolution simulations of the Martian atmosphere, their high computational cost makes them largely unsuitable for studies covering millions of years of orbital evolution. MAIC-2 addresses this gap by utilizing physically-based, zonally-averaged parameterizations, including a Local Insolation Temper

item.title: STORM: A Lightweight Structure-Free Model for Binding Affinity Prediction
item.description:
Authors: Ayush Pandit, Rohan V. Koodli, Wei Deng, Roxana Daneshjou, Ron O. Dror

Accurately predicting a small molecule's binding affinity to a protein, a critical task in drug discovery, remains challenging. Physics-based approaches like free-energy perturbation (FEP) have very high computational costs and require expert setup. Recent machine learning--based cofolding models have reported accuracy approaching that of FEP---and at least one of them, Boltz-2, has already been widely adopted for affinity prediction---but they remain expensive for large computational screens and even more expensive for retraining on newly collected experimental data

item.title: A State-Level Assessment of Space Weather Impact on the Virginia Power Grid: From Vulnerability to Mitigation Strategies
item.description:

item.title: CAFE-AQI: Coverage-Aware Day-Ahead AQI Forecasting with Early Warning and Conformal Uncertainty in Bangladesh
item.description:
Authors: Md Rafid Islam, Rafsan Jany, Rafid Bin Zaman, Mohammad Fahim Islam, Hafiz Abdur Rahman

Next-day air quality forecasting often assumes city records are equally complete and independent. However, an audit of a large Bangladesh dataset revealed a sharp coverage expansion after August 2022 and showed that 103 city labels correspond to only 61 unique AQI trajectories. To address these issues, this paper presents CAFE-AQI, a coverage-aware framework for forecasting next-day maximum AQI

item.title: A System 1 Decision Model for Medical Multiple-Choice Questions Built on Frozen Language Models
item.description:
Authors: Pavan Kumar Mantha

A System 1 model answers a multiple-choice question in a single pass. A frozen language model turns the question and each option into vectors, two small, trained heads place them in a shared space, and the closest option wins. The design has been shown on agent decisions, but we are not aware of a study of how far it goes on exam questions that need medical knowledge, where the right option is often no more similar to the question than the wrong ones
